name: Ad blocker detection
plain: Detects ad blockers via bait elements and filter-list selectors.
meaning: Reveals ad blocker use (about a third of desktop users) and which filter lists (EasyList, AdGuard, Fanboy, regional lists) are on. FingerprintJS probes about 20 lists; list pattern is itself identifying.

web.api: Hidden bait div with ad class names, fetch of ad script URL, selector tests

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if you use an ad blocker and roughly which filter lists
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Test whether bait ads or ad scripts get blocked
Guess which filter lists you have turned on, such as EasyList or AdGuard
Show an ask to turn off your blocker
Use the pattern of blocked items as one clue to tell you apart from other visitors
cannot: See which sites your blocker blocked elsewhere
See your blocker settings directly; it only guesses from results
Be certain; privacy tools can hide the test
limits.reach_label: A guess, while the page loads

story.what_it_is: Checks whether you run an ad blocker, and sometimes which filter lists you use.
story.for_you: You never see the check itself. What you may see is a pop-up that says Please turn off your ad blocker, or an article that stays blurred until you do. Some sites then show less or nothing.
story.for_makers: Sites that live on ad income want to know how many readers block ads. They use the check to ask for an exception, serve a subscription offer or measure lost revenue. Fraud tools also use the exact blocker set as one more clue about a device.

use_cases.example: A news site blurs the article and asks you to disable your blocker or subscribe.
A video platform detects blockers and slows or interrupts playback until ads are allowed.
A free browser games portal shows a polite wall asking you to whitelist the site because ads pay for the games.
An ad recovery service injects a different, less intrusive ad format for people who block normal ads.
A publisher estimates how much revenue is lost to blockers in each country by counting detection hits.
A fingerprinting service adds the blocker and its list choices to a device profile that follows you across sites.

risks: Pressure to turn off privacy tools

technical_bounds: Cannot see which sites were blocked on
